newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lafarge sees 97 sales up more than 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lafarge sees 97 sales up more than 10 pct.

text.p: French building materials group Lafarge said on Wednesday it expected 1997 turnover to be in the order of 39 billion francs, up more than 10 percent than 35.2 billion in 1996.
It gave the figures in a document released with its results.

Lafarge also said it expected to invest between six and eight billion francs in 1997, compared with 7.009 billion in 1996, which would take total investment from the beginning of 1995 to 20 billion francs.
It said it planned to build a plasterboard factory with a capacity of 20 million square metres in Shanghai which would cost $60 million.
Lafarge said the Onada group and Chinese firm Shanghai Shipping would also take part in the project, taking a 38 percent and five percent stake respectively. The factory should open in 1998, it said.
